extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and counsel involved in USPTO reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline at the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority, including service, opportunity to respond, and applicable professional-conduct violations supporting discipline. Focuses on reprimand imposed for failures of diligence and communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO may impose disciplinary action identical to that imposed by a State authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24 (e.g., a reprimand before the USPTO predicated on being reprimanded by a duly constituted authority of a State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24' requesting identical discipline. If the procedural requirements of §11.24 are met and no genuine issue of material fact is raised, reciprocal discipline such as reprimand is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within 40 days to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24 must provide the respondent an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response window is triggered by proper service (see service/mailing requirement). A timely response may raise issues under §11.24(d)(1) to oppose identical discipline; failure to file a response can lead to a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must specify that the respondent may assert those regulatory reasons; the page references the existence of these grounds (but does not list them verbatim). Raising such grounds timely is necessary to create a genuine issue of material fact that could prevent identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact standard under §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the Notice and opportunity to respond, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order here states that in light of the respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined there is no genuine issue of material fact and reprimand is the appropriate discipline. Raising factual disputes in the response is the mechanism to create a genuine issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act with reasonable diligence (Rule 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must act with reasonable diligence in representing clients; failure to do so is professional misconduct (Rule 1.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Grievance Committee stated that 'minimal diligence would require a practitioner to perform routine checks of the USPTO's online filing system at least monthly to monitor the status of clients' cases and ensure adherence to deadlines.' Example misconduct includes missed deadlines, notices of abandonment, multiple petitions to revive, and unnecessary refilings caused by lack of monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to reasonable client requests for information (Rule 1.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must respond to reasonable requests for information from clients; failure constitutes a violation of Rule 1.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Grievance Committee found that the respondent 'failed to respond to reasonable requests for information from the client,' and that failure formed a basis for reprimand. Timely, substantive communication with clients is required to avoid discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory basis for discipline (35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions by the USPTO are taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations provide the legal framework authorizing the Office to impose reciprocal discipline based on state actions; practitioners should be aware that state discipline can trigger USPTO proceedings under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing requirements for Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices and Orders under the reciprocal-discipline process are mailed (here, by certified mail) and delivery is documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail with a receipt number and was delivered on a specific date; proof of mailing/delivery is part of the administrative record and starts the response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline by the OED Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Enrollment and Discipline Director may file a Complaint requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint initiates the USPTO reciprocal-discipline process and identifies the state-imposed discipline and the predicate violations forming the basis for the requested USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability of disciplinary decisions (37 C.F.R. §11.59 / Official Gazette / FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish notices of disciplinary action in the Official Gazette and comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.59; disciplinary decisions are publicly available through the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs publication of a Notice of Reprimand in the Official Gazette and cites a FOIA Reading Room URL where disciplinary decisions are published for public review.
